svg.title: What D-Bus physically is
svg.text: What D-Bus physically is (and is not)
D-Bus is NOT a file of messages and NOT a database. It is one running program (dbus-broker) that ROUTES messages between other running programs.
1. THE PICTURE: separate programs, each with its own memory, connected to one router through a socket

svg.text: who may own / call what, loaded from

text.font-family: DejaVu Sans Mono, Menlo, Consolas, monospace

svg.text: A Unix SOCKET: a file-shaped address. Programs "connect" to it like dialling a number.
Nothing is stored in it; you can't cat it. ls -l shows type "s": srw-rw-rw- … system_bus_socket
It lives in /run (RAM). Recreated at every boot.
Where data is SAVED: each program's own files, not D-Bus
At start-up each program reads its files and re-publishes its objects on D-Bus.
2. ONE QUESTION, STEP BY STEP: bmcweb wants CurrentHostState (for "PowerState" in Redfish)
writes a message into its socket connection:

svg.text: xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host0 → :1.17 and copies the message to connection :1.17
its event loop wakes up, finds the property in ITS OWN memory,

svg.text: into the Redfish JSON it sends to your browser
Takes well under a millisecond. Nothing is written anywhere: the value came from the host state manager's memory. If that program isn't running, step 2 fails with "name has no owner".

text.font-family: DejaVu Sans Mono, Menlo, Consolas, monospace

svg.text: an announcement to EVERYONE subscribed: "PropertiesChanged", "InterfacesAdded", "NameOwnerChanged". The broker copies it to each subscriber; nobody replies.
a file you read/write like a message board?
No. Messages pass through the broker and are gone. The socket file is only the address to connect to.
a database or registry of values?
No. Values live inside each program. Ask the program (through the broker) to get them.
No. Message bytes are copied: sender → broker → receiver, through sockets.
No. When a program exits, its name and objects disappear from the bus at once.
No. The system bus is local to the BMC. bmcweb is the bridge between the network (HTTPS) and D-Bus.
A message ROUTER + a NAME registry + a SECURITY policy, run by dbus-broker, plus an agreed message format.
